correctness.rationale: Define each output by literal one-coordinate deletion and disjointness by sets. For n=14,15, the explicit nonnegative integer weight u_m has total 96,111 and every possible constant-weight-three codeword has total distinct deletion-output weight at least 3. A three-case proof covers separated ones, exactly one adjacent pair, and a consecutive triple including the n=15 terminal exception. Thus every code has at most 32,37 words. The accompanying two fully explicit witness codebooks have exactly 32,37 words; a standalone verifier constructs every deletion and independently checks all 364 and 455 candidate triples and all pairwise disjoint deletion outputs. No inference from solver status, partial experiments, or prior codebooks is needed.

originality.rationale: The primary exact-parameter comparison, Hagiwara and Nation (draft dated 2023-10-12, Theorem 11 and Table 3, printed p.11), leaves both 3-of-n maxima at n=14,15 unknown, while providing upper bounds 32,37 and lower bounds 31,35. Our explicit disjoint-output codebooks attain both upper bounds. The Cullina–Kulkarni–Kiyavash arXiv:1211.4056v1 full text establishes constant-weight coloring and constructions but no claim implying these exact sizes. Exact-parameter, insertion-equivalent, more general bounds and database searches revealed no stronger coverage. A future or unindexed source is a residual risk; search absence is not itself a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A post-2023 or unindexed construction might independently achieve 32 or 37 and precede this result; searched titles, aliases, exact code parameters, and equivalent insertion correction but this does not exhaust private or inaccessible work.
The 2012 conference-paper public day is not independently verifiable from conference dates alone; the dated 2012-11-16 arXiv v1 is used for a conservative source anchor.
